entry_state: Timely and late treaties share final cash but differ in initial recovery recognition. Munich Re disclosures distinguish future acquisition outflows,paid acquisition assets,service recovery and cash,with a complete reported CSM movement and explicit PAA scope differences. Ping An's original and restated2022 balances retain separate report and accounting-basis identities;publication availability and underlying transition measurements remain unresolved. Transition methods follow next.
exit_state: Transition routes depend on group-specific eligibility and admissible information. Full and modified retrospection can share cash yet produce different margins;prescribed nil measurements do not erase known payments. Fair-value transition separately compares group fair value with fulfilment cash flows. Its positive margin is added to the liability while its loss component remains inside FCF;the opening-equity reconciliation continues next.
findings: The transition discussion separates initial-application,transition and public-information dates and does not treat a missing workbook alone as impracticability.
Market-participant transfer value differs from immediate settlement,underlying investment value and FCF;own non-performance risk is explicitly treated differently.
The retrospective examples retain known cash and use separate admissible information views. Equal numeric results in one case do not establish equivalence of the routes.
The fair-value comparison derives liability=max(F,V) for its restricted remaining-coverage case and shows why an onerous liability can exceed group fair value. No new confirmed local defect.
